deep.reconstruction:
Context: cote 154 studies arrangements ('systèmes') of pseudo-lines in a real projective plane X (Σ), its double cover X̃ (a 2-sphere), and how arrangements degenerate ('spécialisations' D → D', where several pseudo-lines become concurrent). The previous page draws arrangements with vertex multiplicities (2, 3, 4, p≥3 ...).

Left column (ending an argument begun on p.26). To each D there are closed 2-cells Δ(D) and quotients Δ'(D), obtained by identifying some boundary points. The identifications are 'artificial' and can be made separately: certain edges of the Δ(D) that are disjoint in Δ(D) come to meet on the boundary of Δ'(D). Two gluings are compared.
(i) Glue the Δ(D) along their common edges but do not make the identifications leading to Δ'(D). This gives a compact surface with boundary S₀.
(ii) Cap each boundary circle of S₀ with a disk Δ_x. This gives a closed compact surface S. Equivalently, contract each capping disk to a point, which gives the surface built from the Δ'(D).
Properties of S₀ as stated: boundary points have order 2 or 3, i.e. two or three cells meet there. Every vertex lies on the boundary. S₀ is essentially S with a small open disk removed around each vertex. Hence the holes of S₀ correspond canonically to the vertices of S. Modern reading: S₀ is the vertex-truncation of a polyhedral surface S (boundary components = links of vertices). Equivalently, S is obtained from S₀ by coning off each boundary circle.

Right column, dated 25.12 (presumably 25 Dec 1983). New programme: study the relation between Pol(D) and Pol(D') when D → D' is a specialization to a more degenerate ('sur-...', reading uncertain) arrangement. First Pol must be defined for a single pseudo-line Δ ⊂ Σ. Two options are proposed: either the set of 'generators/generizations' of Δ (reading uncertain), or a suitable polyhedral structure on Δ.
Key recalled fact: certain combinatorial data of Δ (word uncertain, perhaps 'distinctions' or 'bisections') correspond to the vertices of Δ̃, the preimage of Δ in the double cover X̃. Δ̃ is a closed curve on the sphere, invariant under the antipodal map.
The next page continues. At a vertex s of Δ, the two lifts give two 'rives' (sides) of Δ∖{s}. The specialization D → D' selects one side (the one swept by the degeneration). The antipodal map induces a canonical combinatorial isomorphism between the two arcs of Δ̃'∖{s̃, s̃⁻}. This yields a canonical isomorphism from the side of specializations of D onto a combinatorial segment I(D', s). In modern terms: a local description of the link/star of a degenerate stratum in the stratified space of pseudo-line arrangements (oriented-matroid strata). The generic arrangements adjacent to a degenerate one are organised along a combinatorial interval.
errors: No outright mathematical error is visible. The claim 'each vertex is on the boundary' must refer to vertices of the cells Δ(D) after truncation, not to vertices of the closed surface S. The text is elliptic here.
'Order 2 or 3' for boundary points is asserted without justification on this page; it presumably relies on the local structure of the arrangements established on earlier pages.
Pol(D') is explicitly not yet defined, so the 25.12 programme is only a plan, not a result.

ideas.what: Closed polyhedral surface obtained by gluing cells; truncating at vertices gives a surface with boundary whose holes correspond canonically to vertices; recovered by capping (or contracting) the holes.
ideas.modern_name: vertex truncation / coning off boundary components; link of a vertex
ideas.where_published: Similar 'bouchage de trous' manipulations of surfaces occur in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, dessins) but not this specific construction.

ideas.what: Specialization D → D' of pseudo-line arrangements and the comparison of an associated polyhedral object Pol(D) with Pol(D').
ideas.modern_name: stratification of the space of pseudoline arrangements / oriented matroid strata; adjacency and mutation (triangle flips)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956, flips); Folkman–Lawrence (1978); Goodman–Pollack (1980s); Mnëv (1988); Manin–Schechtman higher Bruhat orders (1989)

ideas.what: Using the double cover X̃ (sphere) of the projective plane and antipodal symmetry to give canonical combinatorial identifications of the two 'sides' of a pseudo-line at a vertex.
ideas.modern_name: lift to S² of the projective arrangement; signed/oriented pseudo-circle arrangements (topological representation of rank-3 oriented matroids)

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes defining a polyhedral object Pol attached to a (possibly degenerate) arrangement and studying functoriality under specialization D → D'. This amounts to a local-link description of degenerate strata in the space of pseudo-line arrangements. It is a stratified-space viewpoint resembling later work on realization spaces and the combinatorial Grassmannian (MacPhersonian) of rank 3. The plan is not carried out on this page.
missed.quote: Il faudrait regarder la relation entre Pol(D) et Pol(D'), quand D → D' ... Il faudrait déjà définir Pol(D'), i.e. Pol(Δ) quand Δ ⊂ Σ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The topology of spaces of rank-3 oriented matroids / pseudoline arrangements (MacPhersonian, Mnëv–Sturmfels type questions) remains active. A historically independent 1983 attempt at a canonical local-structure description could be of interest, but there is no concrete result here.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is working notes: a routine truncation/capping description of a glued surface, plus a dated plan (25.12) to compare polyhedral structures under degeneration of pseudo-line arrangements. The broader project (Grothendieck on pseudo-line arrangement spaces, contemporaneous with Goodman–Pollack and pre-Mnëv) is of historical interest. Nothing on this page is a finished new result.

'surparabolique [?]' – the word after D' is illegible; it may be a term for 'more degenerate'. 'surparabolique' should be treated as unreliable.
'l'ens. des générateurs de Δ' may read 'générisations/généralisations de Δ', which fits the specialization context better.
'circonstances [?]' after the crossed-out word is uncertain; possibly '...istinctions' or 'bissections'.
Margin note near 'consistant' ('ou presque' / 'en gros'?) is illegible.
'(bord ... ...)' after 'surface à bord' is likely '(un ... bord)' or 'à bord (en un sens)'; uncertain.
